metadata.Description: We were about to leave the Idehan Ubari to enter the Al-Hamra Plateau, when we had to find shelter in this boundless sea of sand. The last minutes before setting camp we were surfing up and down the giant dunes chasing the sun setting on the horizon. A moment of peace and silence. The sand dancing with the light changes a thousand colours during a day, but it reaches its pinnacle of splendour as evening approaches. It finally comes alive and finds shape, enveloping you as if to offer protection before the onset of darkness.

metadata.Title: Ace of Fire
metadata.Description:
Kether (Ace) is known as the Crown, symbolizing the primordial point of emanation from which all creation springs and to which all returns. It is the most sublime of the Sephiroth, representing unity, the beginning of all things, and the ultimate connection to the Divine or cosmic spark. In the context of Tarot it symbolizes the highest potential or pure essence, aligning with the "Ace" as a symbol of new beginnings or the seed of potential.

Elemental fire represents transformation, energy, purification, and the driving force of will and spirit, akin to a wand fashioned from a branch that kept sprouting new life. Fire is dynamic and consuming, often associated with the processes of change and the relentless pursuit of spiritual ascension.

When elemental fire interacts with Kether, it can be envisioned as the purest form of spiritual fire meeting the source of all existence - the spark of divine inspiration or enlightenment—a moment of pure awareness where the soul recognizes its origin and its ultimate destiny. 

In more practical terms, this meeting can signify the transformative journey of the soul as it ascends through the various planes of existence, burning away all illusions and impurities to return to the pure, undifferentiated state of Kether. This can be seen as the quintessential alchemical process within one's spiritual journey—transmuting the lead of mundane existence into the gold of enlightened consciousness.
metadata.Haiku:
Fire meets the Crown's light,
Burning paths to purest form—
Soul's gold awakening.

metadata.Title: Ace of Water
metadata.Info:
'o' toggles opacity effect
Glitch effects by GL1TCH C0DE$
metadata.Description:
Kether (Ace) is known as the Crown, symbolizing the primordial point of emanation from which all creation springs and to which all returns. It is the most sublime of the Sephiroth, representing unity, the beginning of all things, and the ultimate connection to the Divine or cosmic spark. In the context of Tarot it symbolizes the highest potential or pure essence, aligning with the "Ace" as a symbol of new beginnings or the seed of potential.

Elemental Water symbolizes the flowing, adaptable nature of life. It represents depth, emotion, intuition, and the unconscious mind. Similar to the cup archetype "The Holy Grail" it is often associated with the mysteries of the soul and the essence of life itself. Water's qualities of reflection, fluidity, and connectivity speak to its role as a nurturer and a binder, making it a critical element in understanding both the human psyche and the natural world.

In this interaction, Water brings its capacity for deep emotional understanding and intuitive knowledge to the realm of Kether, where these elements are purified and elevated. This signifies a process of spiritual cleansing where the murky waters of the subconscious are clarified and aligned with the cosmic will. It's akin to the mystical process of the dissolution of the false self and the emergence of the true self in the pure awareness of the divine.

The energy signature of Water meeting Kether is thus one of profound spiritual renewal and the infinite depths of divine love and compassion.
metadata.Haiku:
In the cosmic crown's embrace,
Water's depths reflect divine,
Souls cleansed in sacred space.

metadata.context: How would it look like, to see the world tender again. Weaken its impulses that are wreaking havoc upon the soul of oneself - upon the mind. Fighting spirits or are we spirits fighting for - for what exactly. Survival?! To what extent one has to hurt another before realizing their own weakness in doing so? Motives to enrich - to grow in a stampede. Suspecting eternal happiness from taking on actions restraining others. Is it religious, moral, fundamental or philosophical differences? Are those so key to defer and denounce? There could have been moments when it was worth to blow a whistle. See the lifeguard run towards the border of the reservoir - overlooking the ephermal border identifed as a 'nation 'in distance and lamenting. But is there really anyone to save us? Us or them is often the question. Take on the vest and act with courage - whistleblow and cherish. Some believe in good - of spirits, and share positive energy. Be the lifeguard and see past the borders. Past the pain. Reconnect with peers.
